text:
maria: FYI noticed a weird accuracy jitter when we switch precision mid-context on the long-chat workload. latency looks fine but next-token probs wobble around token 512 onward.

olga: can you paste the tiny repro / logs? is this when we hot-swap from FP8 -> 4-bit?

maria: yeah, usually FP8 -> int4 after a prefix. quick repro: we run a long prompt, enable LDP-profile per-layer after N tokens, and the token probs shift. snippet:```python
# pseudo runtime switch
if token_idx == 256:
    runtime.set_precision(profile="int4_per_layer")
```
Not sure if it's KV-cache alignment or activation-range mismatch.

raj: sounds like an "activation stitching" problem — when you quantize activations/kv across two precision regimes the scale/zero-point (or fp8 exponent bias) mismatch can induce distribution shift. two ways to think about it: 1) do a per-segment affine remap of activations during the switch (store scale/shift for last subbatch) 2) avoid cross-segment switches unless calibration indicates safe continuity. tradeoffs: mapping removes discontinuity but adds bias and requires extra compute and memory to store segment stats.

olga: what telemetry would prove it's the scale mismatch vs algorithmic degeneracy? propose: emit per-segment activation histograms + cross-segment KL (activation distribution before vs after switch), and token-level logprob delta / perplexity delta for the next 8 tokens. if KL > 0.02 or avg logprob drop > 0.5 then mark as "stitch-failed".

sam: runtime-wise this is tricky. extra histograms per request will hit TC / tail latency. alternative: compute lightweight 64-bin sketches or run calibration on a sampled microbatch (1/10 requests). also consider policy: if a model artifact includes a `quant_stitch_safe` flag, runtime can skip costly checks. otherwise default conservative: pin precision for contiguous prefixes.

maria: +1 on sketches. also propose a compact on-disk artifact hint: `quant_profile_hints` with small vectors: last_segment_scale, last_segment_bias, preferred_granularity (per-channel|per-tensor). example:```json
{"quant_profile_hints": {"last_scale": "[0.023,0.045,..]", "granularity":"per_channel"}}
```
This could let runtime apply a cheap affine correction when switching.

raj: operational fallback: if the cheap correction doesn't reduce the KL below threshold, automatically roll to higher-precision for next M tokens (configurable, e.g., M=64), and emit an alert for model-team review. That keeps availability while we collect richer telemetry for an RFC.

deploy-bot: canary: quant-stitching-sketches enabled on canary fleet (tag: canary/quant-stitch) :rocket:

olga: next steps: 1) write RFC that outlines: activation-stitch affine remap, cheap sketch telemetry, artifact hint API, and fallback policy. 2) add unit tests that synthesize a known scale mismatch and ensure remap brings KL < threshold. 3) add end-to-end microbench to measure overhead.

maria: i'll draft the RFC and ping model-ops. assigning owners: maria (draft), olga (telemetry), raj (runtime policy), sam (perf microbench). will post link in #eng-ml when ready. :thumbsup:
